reason: The docs quickstart converts a PyTorch model to Core AI IR, compiles it and runs inference locally; a manylinux coreai-core wheel exists, and no keys or gated downloads are needed.
demo: docs/getting-started/quickstart.ipynb (Define, Export, Decompose, Convert, Compile and Run) plus README Usage
goal: Install coreai-torch from the cloned repo (coreai-core==1.0.0b3 and torch come from PyPI; Python >=3.11 is required, CPU-only torch is fine). Then run the quickstart pipeline on CPU: export a small nn.Module with torch.export, run_decompositions(get_decomp_table()), convert with TorchConverter().add_exported_program(...).to_coreai(), save_asset to an .aimodel, load the executable and run function 'main' via coreai.runtime.NDArray. The Core AI output must match PyTorch. Put the environment setup in /work/env.sh (activating it must make `python` import coreai_torch).
check: A script converts, compiles and runs a small MLP through Core AI and checks that the output matches PyTorch within 1e-4.
